prompt: I need to find out where our C++ ingest service spends its time. It's built with `cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` (so -O3 -DNDEBUG), and the benchmark run is `./build/bin/ingest --replay traces/day1.bin`, which takes about 40 s. It runs on an Ubuntu 24.04 Xeon server; I'll run the commands there myself (you don't have access to it). Give me the exact commands to run, in order, and tell me what to look for in each output.
assertions: The plan adds debug info without changing the optimization level being profiled: it keeps -O3 (e.g. adds -g to CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS or CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE) and does not switch to RelWithDebInfo or -O2, or, if it mentions RelWithDebInfo, it warns that this changes -O3 to -O2.
The plan includes a step to check perf_event_paranoid (or otherwise check perf permissions) before collecting, and says what to do if it's too restrictive (run with sudo or lower the setting).
The plan includes a perf stat counting pass (cycles, instructions, cache and branch events) and explains how to read IPC and the miss rates from it.

The plan includes perf record with call-graph collection that works on an -O3 build without frame pointers (`--call-graph dwarf` or `lbr`, or rebuilding with -fno-omit-frame-pointer) and perf report to rank the hot functions.
The plan includes perf annotate (or perf report's annotate view) to drill into the hottest functions at the source-line or instruction level.
